instruction: Hello doctor,I had mumps five months ago and after that, I started to have an infection in my left testes. It was swollen and now it has shrunk to almost half the size of the other one. As I am sexually active, I feel a pain in each of the vas deferens after sex. If I do not have sex for days, they become sensitive. I was treated with Ceftum 500 mg, the first time I had an infection. Now my question is, is there any chance that the infection is still in my body? And, do I need to get examined for it? For the time being, please suggest some precautionary antibiotics for my relief.
output: 1) There is no need to worry about reinfection as the infection caused by Mumps virus does not persist in the body and is completely cleared up by the immune system.2) The swelling at your scrotum is due to inflammation of epididymis or vas deferens which is a result of mumps infection.3) There is no need to take antibiotics for this problem. You can take anti-inflammatory medicines like Ibuprofen for symptomatic relief.4) Doing cool compresses over the scrotal area will help in reducing the inflammation and pain.

instruction: Hello doctor,I am trying to conceive but my husband and I did cocaine a week ago. How long should my husband and I wait to safely continue to try to get pregnant? How long until it is out of our system? How long does cocaine stay in sperm? Thanks in advance.
output: 1) Cocaine use can affect fertility by causing male infertility due to decreased sperm motility and morphology as well as increased abnormal semen parameters (especially pH). However, there is insufficient evidence to suggest that cocaine causes significant changes in female fertility.2) It is not clear how long cocaine remains in semen or blood after use. Therefore, it is difficult to say exactly when it will be completely gone from your husbands body.3) There is no data regarding the amount of time that couples need to abstain from sexual activity before attempting conception.4) In conclusion, if you want to become pregnant, then you should avoid coke for at least three months before trying to conceive. Hope this helps

instruction: Hello doctor,I need advice after my second CT chest result. Six months back, I went for a CT scan because I have got chest pain which suddenly comes and goes and I wanted to go for a check-up. The CT showed a right-sided nodule measuring 3 mm and was advised to RPT interval scan in six months. I have done the second CT, the previous nodule is still there and they found another one.In the LLL, a 4 mm nodule is representative of an intrapulmonary lymph node. No suspicious lung lesion. Tiny 3 mm RLL nodule noted. No enlarged lymph nodes. Mild thymic hyperplasia. The partly visualized upper abdominal viscera appear unremarkable. No aggressive bony lesion. They said I do not need to do anything which is strange because there are two nodes now and the second one was not there six months ago. Do I need some kind of medicine therapy to clear my lung from this node or do I need to check if it is growing or not after one year?
output: 1) The nodules are probably benign and unlikely to grow.2) There is no reason to worry about them at present.3) You may be monitored with CT scans every 6 months to see if they change in size or number.4) If they do change, then biopsy of these nodules can be done to determine whether they are cancerous or not.5) At present, you should just continue to follow up with CT scans every 6 months.

instruction: Hello doctor,I am a 50-year-old female who has had an elevated ferritin level for many years now. My last ferritin level was 342, 20 days back. My ferritin level has been as high as 390. I think your doctors are rightly treating this condition by monitoring iron levels, but do not ignore your symptoms. 4) You should consult a psychiatrist who might prescribe medicines like pregabalin or duloxetine for fibromyalgia.

instruction: Hi doctor,I am a 25-year-old male. I do not have any medical history. Been always healthy. For the past 3 months, I have been experiencing this facial tightness which comes pretty often throughout the day with different intensity. The facial tension usually comes half an hour after I leave the bed. The tightness on my face happens to be on both sides of my face but usually more intense on the right. At times, I can feel it from my neck all the way up to my face. As of recent, I have been feeling this slight burning sensation on my chest to my shoulders as well. Prior to this facial tightness, I have been suffering from this burning feeling on the centre of my chest for about a month. It was my first time experiencing heartburn and I thought it was heart related. Went for X-rays and echo heart ultrasound. Everything came out fine. I have a healthy heart. What made the burning chest sensation go away temporarily is lying down, eating, exercising and drinking alcohol. And the weird part is the same thing helps me relieve my facial tightness temporarily is the same thing as that for the burning chest sensation; lying down, eating, exercising and drinking alcohol.Since having this facial tightness, I have paid numerous visits to different doctors, even the neuro-specialist and they all said it was anxiety. The doctors did facial senses test where they take a piece of fine cotton to touch different parts of my face. I had to close my eyes and tell them where the spot is. I have no troubles at all. I did blood test. It came out normal. They told me I do not need to do any scans and that it was merely anxiety and it will go off by itself. I convinced myself that I had anxiety because of the one month heartburn ordeal that I was suffering from. Even though the facial tightness was there, I tried my utmost best to ignore it. I do not think that I have any anxiety in me now as I try not to think of the weird tightness sensation. However, it has been 3 whole months and now I am getting alarmed and worried that it is still here and with newer sensations as I described above. In all honesty, I do feel that the intensity of the facial tension as compared to I first experienced it, is less. However, it is always there even as when I am typing this. I do not see any physical change on my body. Not sure if it is neuro damage. I am worried sick.Hope I can get some form of advice and diagnosis.
output: 1) Burning sensation on your chest could be due to acid reflux disease (GERD). This is a common condition where the gastric juices flows back into esophagus and causes discomfort. 2) Facial tightness can be due to muscle spasm. 3) Neither of these conditions are caused by anxiety. You should visit a physician who would examine you and then decide what tests he wants to order.

instruction: Hello doctor,My mother is 75 years old. She had been treated for TB (tuberculosis) of the abdomen as her ultrasound of abdomen finding was thicken bowel loop. instruction: Hello doctor,My son has developed anxiety symptoms about four years ago. They came completely out of the blue. We ran a battery of tests when it first happened including TSH, EKG, lung scans, blood panels, etc. and everything was normal. So we went down the path of anxiety. Four years later, the symptoms continued. As my son now has a terrible fear of doctors, we tried a home blood test to get a full thyroid panel. I have attached the results.The blood work came back normal. Low normal TSH, but low normal T4 and lower normal free T4 and free T3. There is nothing that shows an abnormality. However, his urine test showed moderately low iodine and slightly low selenium. I have read that abnormalities in these measures could cause thyroid problems. What am I wondering is if these two indicators are worth further exploration with an endocrinologist knowing that going to the doctor will cause my son a severe panic.Also, is it possible that low iodine could have been a temporary diet thing and it is masking the signs of hyperthyroidism in the blood work? He has all of the symptoms of someone with hyperthyroidism. On a side note, I am hypothyroid, my sister is hypothyroid and my two nieces had Hashimoto\s with my younger niece having thyroid cancer and got her thyroid removed at age of 22. So everyone on my side of the family has thyroid issues. We were wondering if you could please give us some guidance. Looking to see if we need to eliminate thyroid as a possible cause of his symptoms or if it is worth further pursuit.
output: Hi, Thanks for writing in. The blood levels of thyroid hormones are not always accurate in people with anxiety. In such cases, an ultrasound scan of the neck can be done which can help in differentiating between a normal thyroid gland and enlargement of the thyroid gland due to inflammation or goiter. In case of enlargement of the thyroid gland, the treatment is simple. It consists of taking anti-inflammatory medicines like steroids along with thyroxine. This is called as subclinical hyperthyroidism. In case of thyroiditis, the thyroid function tests may come back normal but there might be some changes seen on thyroid ultrasound. These are transient conditions and resolve over a period of time without any specific treatment. Do discuss the above with your doctor. Hope this helps.

instruction: Hi doctor,I am a 49-year-old woman and last month I was hospitalized with a necrotizing soft tissue infection on my thigh. I went to an urgent care and was prescribed Clindamycin and told to return in three days for drainage. The abscess did not improve or get worse over the three days. I got it drained and was prescribed Augmentin and told to also continue the clindamycin. That was a week ago and the wound is healing well. output: 1) MRSA is a superbug and is resistant to most of the antibiotics in use today. It is spread through direct contact with the skin lesions of someone carrying the bug or through contact with contaminated surfaces. Most hospitals routinely screen patients for MRSA colonization of their nasal cavity, mouth, and anal region.2) MRSA is usually resistant to penicillin and vancomycin, so if your infections were treated with those medications then you probably didn't have MRSA.3) You can take measures to avoid getting MRSA again like using hand sanitizer frequently, keeping your hands clean, doing regular baths with bleach water, avoiding contact with people who have visible skin lesions, wearing gloves when touching broken skin, etc. Hope this helps

instruction: Hi doctor,What is the difference between IntraLasik and Contoura Lasik?

The main differences between these two procedures include the type of laser used, the amount of tissue removed, the accuracy of the procedure, the depth of correction possible, and the cost. IntraLASIK uses a femtosecond laser instead of a microkeratome to create a flap in the cornea. This laser is more precise than the microkeratome and can be programmed for individualized treatment plans. It also allows for greater depth of correction and is considered safer because it eliminates the possibility of an accidental cut caused by the microkeratome. instruction: Hello doctor,I am a 25-year-old male. My bpm is 31 during physical and mental exhaustion but my bpm is high of about 178 during hyperventilation and has pointless frustration. My bpm from rest to stand increases by at least 30 points but averages a 50 point increase. My resting bpm is 40, and upon standing it increases to 90 and peaks up to 110.I had done an echo cardiogram and EKG. I feel light-headed upon standing, along with sudden pulsation, headache and muscle spasms. I feel blackout, syncope, and fainting. I had spontaneous jolt, breathless, palpitations, flutters, fatigue, chills and skin rash on the back of hands.My mental disturbances include confusion, inability to maintain thoughts. I also feel pointless random irritability, ankle pain, random lapse of balance, throbbing extremities, vibrating vision, burning sensation, social anxiety, depression, irritating bowl movements, no appetite and chest discomfort.I wast told to mention the possibility of autonomic dysfunction as its often times overlooked.
output: Hi, Thanks for writing in. You have mentioned that your heart rate increases significantly when you stand up after sitting down. This is called orthostatic hypotension or postural hypotension. It occurs because blood vessels dilate while you are lying down and constrict when you stand up leading to low blood pressure. There may be other causes like anemia, thyroid problems etc. which can cause similar symptoms. You need to get evaluated properly to know what is causing this problem. You should wear a monitor which records your heart rhythm continuously for 24 hours. This will help us find out if there is any abnormality in your heart rhythm.

instruction: Hello doctor,My 4 years old daughter has an inward turn in her right eye after concentrating for a while. We had an eye test recently. Can you tell me if her results mean she needs glasses as she keeps saying her eyes hurt watching television and readings of her results are: Right eye sph +1.50 cyl -0.50, left eye sph +1.50 cyl -0.50. They told me she is long sighted and we have a strong family history of squints and glasses. I do not know if I should get a second opinion.
output: 1. Long-sightedness (hyperopia) means that light focuses behind your eye, instead of on it. This causes objects to appear blurred unless they are very close to your face.2. Short-sightedness (myopia) means that light focuses in front of your eye, instead of on it. This causes distant objects to appear blurred.3. Astigmatism is when the shape of the cornea or lens of your eye is irregular, causing light to be focused at two points rather than one point. This causes objects to look blurry at all distances.4. Eye strain can cause headaches, tiredness, and other symptoms. These symptoms usually improve with resting your eyes.5. In my opinion your child need to wear glasses for both the eyes. But you can take second opinion from another opthalmologist before taking any action.

instruction: Hello doctor,I am a 62-year-old male. I went for a routine X-ray, and the radiologist found some streakiness in the lower left lung. He said it appeared small and not significant, but it was adviced that I should come back in six months for a comparative X-ray and that it could just be a scar from an earlier infection.I have read that a small scar area is probably non-progressive but I have also read about IPF, and that fills me with fear. Spirometry test was normal as it was a physical exam. I am so scared that it might be a progressive disease, but I hope that it is just an old scar as it is really small. Otherwise mostly healthy with no cough or difficulty breathing at all. Are all lung scars progressive?
output: 1) Yes, all scars are potentially progressive. However, there are many different types of scarring and they don't all behave the same way. The most common type of scar seen in lungs (and other organs) is called fibrosis. This is when the body repairs itself by forming collagen, which forms dense tissue. Fibrotic scars can be very bad if they form too much collagen, however this doesn't happen in most cases.2) Your doctor was correct to say that this was likely due to an old infection. Infections can cause some degree of scarring, and these are usually reversible.3) It is possible that your scarring is related to IPF, but this would require further testing such as CT scan or bronchoscopy to rule out other causes. You will need to see your doctor again for a repeat chest x-ray and possibly a pulmonary function test.

instruction: Hello doctor,No one is diabetic in my whole family. My sugar levels are fluctuating. I have never taken any medicine for diabetes.
output: 110 mg / dL (6.1 mmol / L) fasting blood glucose level is normal. That means your body is able to produce sufficient insulin to maintain your blood glucose at this level after not eating for about 10 hours. You should check your blood glucose again between 45 minutes and 90 minutes after eating something containing carbohydrates. It will be higher than the fasting level. This rise in blood glucose is due to the action of insulin which your body produces to digest the food. After that it should come down again to the fasting level within two hours. This is called the peak response or the area under curve (AUC). The AUC value can help to know how well your body is responding to the insulin produced by the pancreas. The AUC values of more than 80% are considered good.

instruction: Hi doctor,I do a couple of sports to have some hip flexibility. I am pretty flexible, and I can do right and left splits. output: Hi, Thanks for writing in. The center split you are referring to is called as the "splitting" of the leg. This is done by rotating the foot inwards while keeping the knee straight. When you do this, your whole body weight gets transferred to the front side of the knee. This is where the pain originates from. When you rotate the knee backwards and hips forward, the pressure is shifted to the other side and hence the pain reduces. It is possible to reduce the pain through stretching exercises. You should start with gentle stretching of the groin muscles and then gradually move onto full splits. However, if the pain persists even after adequate stretching, you may need to consult a physician who will advise you further investigations like X-ray, MRI etc. In case it is a ligament injury, physical therapy along with medicines will help.

The reason is that it can detect better any abnormality in the heart function which may be missed in the routine echo. On the other hand, the regular echo is still needed as a screening tool to exclude possible heart valve problems. As far as the family history is concerned, it does increase the risk of coronary artery disease. You should try to control your cholesterol levels and blood pressure as much as possible. In addition, I recommend having an annual physical check up including a resting ECG and lipid profile. Hope to have been helpful. Let me know if I can assist you further. Kind regards,

instruction: Hello doctor,My wife has lung cancer PD-L1. I need your advice regarding the continuation of this therapy. Docetaxel and Nintedanib are suggested. I think it is too heavy. I would prefer immunotherapy, if possible.
output: In the treatment of lung cancer, immunotherapy is not yet approved by FDA for being used as a first line treatment. The only available immunotherapies for lung cancer are nivolumab and pembrolizumab which are both approved by FDA. They are used in patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) who have progressed after platinum-based chemotherapy and targeted therapy (tyrosine kinase inhibitors). These treatments may also be given to people whose cancer has worsened after surgery or radiation therapy. These medicines are usually used in combination with another type of medicine called an antiangiogenic (such as cediranib). There is very limited evidence that any of these treatments will help slow down the spread of the disease.

instruction: Hello doctor,I am 18 years old and I once in my lifetime applied toothpaste on my bottom eyelid trying to help with the dark circles I had but then I had an irritation there and the next morning I had a scab which later fell off and left an indentation on my end eye that looks like an ugly wrinkle. output: Hi welcome to Chat Doctor forum.  Thanks for your query. The upper lids do not have any glands or sebaceous glands, so they cannot get infected by applying anything over them. But the lower lids have a very rich supply of sebaceous glands. They can get infected easily as well if you apply some ointment or creams over them. So please avoid such applications in the future. I hope this information helps you. Thank you

instruction: Hello doctor,I believe I am having a few genital warts, for which I tried some home remedies as well as wart freeze away recently. Why there is redness around them? What are the possible ways to get rid of it?

instruction: Hi doctor,My daughter has pleural infection in lungs. When she was 2 years, decortication was done by open surgery. Now she is four years old. 3 days back she got fever. Though after taking antibiotic her fever subsided, x-ray report showed mild cardiomegaly with bilateral perihilar congestion. Is there again a chance for fluid to get gathered inside her lungs? What should we do for the same? Please advice.
output: 1. The possibility of recurrence of pleural effusion is very low if she had no episodes since then.2. However, it is possible that she might be having some other condition like pneumonia or bronchitis which would cause chest infection and lead to cardiac enlargement.3. For this reason, I suggest you consult your pediatrician for clinical examination and further investigations (like ECG, echocardiography) so that appropriate treatment can be started.

instruction: Hi doctor,I am losing my hair day by day. Can I use Finasteride? I have hydrocele. Is it related to my testosterone?
output: Hi, Yes, it is possible to use finasteride for your condition. It is not related to the testosterone level in blood. But, there might be some relation between testosterone and hair loss in general. But, this is still controversial. You can try finasteride, but if it does not work, then you can go for other options like minoxidil and/or platelet-rich plasma therapy. Hope this helps.

instruction: Hello doctor,I have got round dark spots on face. It was light initially and became darker later on. Give me advice on how to remove it.
output: 1) You need to have your blood sugar levels checked as diabetes can cause these pigmentation marks.2) Also, you might be having an allergic reaction which is causing this skin pigmentation.3) I would suggest that you start using a mild steroid cream like fluticasone or triamcinolone acetone ointment at night for about two weeks.4) If the problem persists then visit a dermatologist who will recommend a stronger steroid cream or oral medications if needed.5) I hope this helps you. Wish you good health.

instruction: Hello doctor, How accurate are early ultrasounds at determining gestational age and conception? Based on my 6th-week scan I am 23 weeks today means I conceived around December 25th. Is it possible that I actually conceived around December 5th and baby is measuring small? (I have had six ultrasounds and the baby has never measured more than 2 days off from the date given at my 6-week scan) even though my last period last came on November 28th she has never measured on track for that.
output: Hi Dear, Welcome to Chat Doctor forum. As you rightly said, an Ultrasonography can be done only after 6 weeks of pregnancy, as before that there is no way to find out about the pregnancy. The most reliable method for detection of pregnancy is Hormone assay in blood serum. Your dates may not be correct, if your periods were irregular, or if the dates were miscalculated. Please consult your Gynecologist for confirmation of your dates. Wishing you a very Good Health. Thank you.

instruction: Hi doctor,What is polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia? Can it be related to leukemia?
output: Hi there, Polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia is a condition in which your body produces too many antibodies or immunoglobulins (IgG). It can also occur with leukemia. But this is not always the case and it does not mean that you have leukemia just because you have polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia. You should get an evaluation by your doctor who will look for signs of leukemia such as fever, bone pain, night sweats etc. Hope I could help nourishing you good health.

instruction: Hi doctor,Over six months I have had what was thought to be an epidermoid cyst at the end of the right side of my nose. I have taken antibiotics on a regular basis as there is redness, swelling and tenderness in the area when inflamed. Approximately 2 weeks ago this cyst on my nose became very inflamed or infected. I was experiencing headache, sore neck, painful and uncomfortable nose and facial pressure (swelling), pressure in my ears and dry infected eye that too right side consequently. I visited GP and had CT scan of paranasal sinuses. I hope you could provide me the explanation for the below sentence, which I am unable to understand. The nasal septum deviates towards the right associated with a large right sided bony spur which abuts the right middle turbinate. Pneumatization of the left middle turbinate (concha bullosa) noted. In simple terms what does this mean? What is the likely recommended action for this? Are these comments and findings consistent with the symptoms I have experienced?
output: Hi thanks for your question. Nasal septum deviation and turbinectomy is commonly seen in chronic rhinosinusitis patients. It means that the septum has shifted toward the right side due to chronic inflammation of the sinus. The turbinates are also enlarged due to same reason. Turbinate enlargement causes congestion and sinus obstruction leading to headache, facial pressure etc. You will need surgery to correct the septum deviation and turbinectomy. Hope this helps. Regards

instruction: Hello doctor,I have my niece with red islands or patches on the tongue surface. Her age is 23 months. This is there for the past one year.
output: 1) These lesions can be due to trauma or irritation of the tongue.2) It may also be due to vitamin B deficiency.3) The lesion can also be secondary to an infection or allergy.4) I would suggest that you consult your pediatrician and get it evaluated.5) To confirm the diagnosis, you can take a biopsy sample of the lesion and send it to the laboratory for examination under the microscope. Hope this helps.

instruction: Hello doctor,I had my last periods two months back. instruction: Hi doctor,I am 31 years old and a mother of 7 months old baby. Recently, I have got infected with herpes zoster virus on my back. It is a small patch above my waist. Doctor told me to stop breastfeeding for a week. But, my baby is exclusively breastfed till now and not taking bottle feed after several attempts. My question is should I completely stop breastfeeding? Will breast milk transfer chickenpox virus? I am eagerly waiting for your response.
output: 1) The infection you have developed is caused by Herpes Zoster which is a virus and it cannot be transmitted from one person to another through breast milk.2) However, if you want to be absolutely sure that there is no transmission of disease through your breast milk then you can express the milk using a sterile technique (using a clean glass and a filter) and discard the expressed milk.

instruction: Hello doctor,It is said that "oral absorption of isotretinoin is enhanced when given with a high-fat meal." My meal, while on Accutane just has normal fat. Does it affect the absorption?
output: 1) Yes, if you have a high fat meal it will enhance the absorption of Isotretinoin.2) But, it is not necessary that every time you take an oral medication along with food, it will increase its absorption.3) The amount of fat in your diet should be less than 30% of total calorie intake.4) You can discuss this with your treating Doctor.

instruction: Hello doctor,I had a tooth extraction done nine days ago top left #14 and my gums are still swollen. It looks like a white blister around the extraction site. My dentist will not listen to me and the pain I am in. Is it something I should worry about? It is causing pain too.

instruction: Hello doctor,My eosinophils are increased to 7. It is very difficult to breathe. An effective treatment to eosinophilia may be communicated.

instruction: Hi doctor,My father had mild chest pain. The doctor did an angiogram, and they told there is a block in the blood pumping vessel and it is closed. We planned for placing a stent. The next day, the doctor tested again and told the blood vessel is opened and it is normal. So, the stent was not placed. After a few days, my father had pain below the heart which was on the rib side, and he told something is holding in the heart. So, again we went to the cardiologist. The doctor examined him and said he is fine and there is nothing to worry. Whenever he got this pain, we consulted the cardiologist, and he said there is no problem in the heart. He got this pain for about three times till now. Again, we tested for a gastric problem and a neurological problem. That was also fine after the examination. But, still he is experiencing the same pain, and he is willing to do angiogram now. I cannot understand the problem. Please suggest.
output: 1. Mild chest pain with angina like symptoms can be due to many causes like coronary artery disease, pericarditis, pleurisy etc.2. Angiography will help rule out all these causes.3. As your father has been diagnosed as having CAD (Coronary Artery Disease) earlier, I would advise you to get his ECG done before going for angiography as it will help us know if any blockage is present or not.4. Pain below the heart can be due to pleuritic changes.5. Gastric problem and neurological problem need to be ruled out by doing relevant investigations.6. You can discuss with your treating Doctor regarding the above points.

instruction: Hello doctor,I am a 32-year-old, male, 105 kg, 6 feet in height. Recently, I have been diagnosed with diabetes. I am not on any medication. I am strictly controlling food and doing regular aerobic exercises. My one hour postprandial BG is always around 200.

instruction: Hello doctor,Can I take Testosterone cypionate and Trenbolone enanthate, while on high blood pressure medication Benicar 20 mg?

It is better if you consult your doctor or physician first before taking these hormones.4. instruction: Hello doctor,My vaginal opening is white in color and it itches a lot around that area. It has been like this only for the past 4 to 5 days.

The rest of your body parts do not have any contact with mucous membranes and hence, they cannot transmit the virus. So, even though you had a very small amount of secretions on your penis, the risk of transmission of HIV is negligible. Now coming to your other doubt, yes, moist

instruction: Hello doctor,I have gallbladder mass and jaundice. Please help.
output: 1. I am sorry to hear about your medical condition.2. The most important thing is that you should get an ultrasound abdomen done to confirm the diagnosis of gall bladder mass with cholecystitis.3. It is not possible to give any treatment without knowing what type of gall bladder mass it is.4. In case if it is benign then it can be managed conservatively by surgery or laparoscopic cholecystectomy.5. In case of malignant lesion then chemotherapy or radiotherapy will be needed.6. Get examined by a surgeon for further management.

instruction: Hello doctor,How likely is a CAT scan to show a lung cancer if a pleural effusion is present? My husband has a pleural effusion and has had four CT scans, none of which show any suspicious mass. Cytology records are inconclusive. I am wondering if the presence of the pleural effusion limits the visibility of a potential tumor? What about in the presence of a middle lobe collapse, could that be hiding a tumor? He has right side pain, short of breath, and was admitted to hospital and fluid drained.
output: Hi, Thanks for writing in. A CT scan does not always pick up a lung cancer even with a pleural effusion. There are many reasons why it may not be detected. The most common reason being the size of the lesion or its location. Also, there are other causes of pleural effusions like tuberculosis, pneumonia etc. So first you need to get his chest x-ray done to rule out these conditions. Then he needs to undergo an ECG and echocardiography to rule out heart diseases. And then only a thoracotomy can tell whether there is a malignant growth or not.

instruction: Hello doctor,My 2 year 9 months old daughter was tested and she has an egg white allergy. She ate scrambled eggs accidentally. Should I worry? Is it a problem if the egg is scrambled? Please, can you advise?
output: Hi, Welcome to Chat Doctor forum. Egg whites contain high levels of protein that have been associated with allergic reactions in some individuals. In general, eggs are considered safe for infants when they are processed properly. It is best to avoid eating raw or lightly cooked eggs because of the risk of salmonellosis. Scrambled eggs should be fine as long as there is no cross-contamination from other foods. Hope this answers your query.

instruction: Hello doctor,The level of anti-TPO antibodies is 492. The doctors say it is a state of euthyroid. I am worried about my prognosis. I am a medical student, can I still become a surgeon?
output: 1) Yes, you can be a surgeon, however, there will be some limitations in your profession. You must take care that you don't get exposed to radiation and other chemicals which may cause dysfunction of thyroid gland.2) Also, if you have any problems with ovarian function or menstrual irregularities then this should also be monitored closely as these might be due to hyperthyroidism.3) Your TPO levels indicate that you might be suffering from Hashimoto thyroiditis. This condition can be managed by taking levothyroxine, a synthetic hormone. You need to check your TSH levels every month for at least 6 months to see how well your medicine is working. Hope this helps

instruction: Hi doctor,I ate my dinner yesterday, and a bit of my molar tooth fell out from my mouth. I do not know whether it is a filling or an actual tooth. In your case, it seems that you have developed an abscess which has ruptured leading to dislodgement of the filling/tooth.4. You need to get evaluated by the dentist at the earliest as the condition is worsening with time.5. Treatment will depend upon how much of the tooth is left.

instruction: Hi doctor,A few days ago I was diagnosed with UTI infection. I was put on antibiotics, and the ER doctor sent my urine for a culture. My doctor told me that Klebsiella pneumoniae is present in my urine culture and referred me to a specialist. What does it mean? I am 23 years old and sexually active. Will this bacteria cause harm? This year I have had about four UTIs, which is not normal for me. I am done taking the course of antibiotics. I was given a five-day course. Could this be because the antibiotics are not treating it? Is this curable? Is it contagious? Should I stay away from sexual activity? I am trying to get pregnant. Please help.
output: 1stly don't worry, k. Pneumoniae is a very common gram negative organism, and it can be found in many people without causing any problem. It's only when there is an immunocompromised condition or if the organism multiplies in large numbers then it causes disease. So just keep your fluid intake high, take care of your hygiene and avoid unnecessary use of antiseptic soaps. Your symptoms are suggestive of recurrent UTI, but it may also be due to some other reason like stone in ureter or renal tract infection. Avoid sexual intercourse till you get cured completely. You should visit a urologist and get yourself examined.

instruction: Hello doctor,I am a 65-year-old white male and tested negative for HIV 1 and 2 in a one-time test three to four years ago. I am not sure if it was a third or fourth generation test. I tested negative with a fourth generation test four months back because I thought I might be having some symptoms. And I remembered the flu-like illness about six months after exposure.I weighed 204 kg three months back and now I weigh 191 kg. I have worried a lot (pacing the floor, sleep loss) for past five months, took Paxil, and realized my worry could account for some weight loss. Shortly, after the test, I had the following symptoms:I started having a small patch of 8 to 10 pinpoint sized pink-light red dots under the skin of my left wrist that have been there for two to three weeks.I also had a smooth, flat spot about 3/8 inch in diameter that appeared on the back of my right hand about a week ago, that has now faded to a pinkish brown. I have read about Kaposi sarcoma being a definer of AIDS, but do not understand how that could happen with a non-reactive fourth generation test four months back.Three months back, I had sinus type headaches multiple times that would sometimes be severe. After three rounds of antibiotics and a CT scan two months back that showed shadowing in a sinus, my ENT doctor just told me this week that there is something in my sphenoid sinus. He is treating it with a rinse for inflammation for three weeks before I see him again. I have had blood in my mucous from my nose for past three months. It dries out in my nose and causes blood almost every time I pick at it. The ENT doctor said that the lining of my nose had been worn down from this, but did not seem concerned about it. I do mess with it a lot, and blow my nose a lot.My PSA elevated quickly in the last six months, going from 1.2 to 3.5. A biopsy two months back showed an early cancer in one of the 12 regions biopsied.I had a lithotripsy on an 8 mm kidney stone this month and I am still passing dark urine. I was told that I do have several small stones still in each kidney. I have had multiple stones over the years.I have a swelling sensation all the way around my waist down into my groin at times that has been there for about two months, but no noticeable swelling. Several doctors have felt in my abdomen and detected nothing abnormal. A CT scan with no contrast 10 days ago showed no abnormalities other than a little swelling in the right kidney where the 8 mm stone was blocking the passage into the ureter. A CT with contrast five months back was normal except for showing stones. But I have microscopic blood in my urine since then.My vital signs have consistently been normal for past five months, including temperature, BP and oxygen. I know I am getting old and some of these symptoms happen with age. But it is driving me crazy that so much has happened since my negative fourth generation test which is supposed to detect antibodies may not be conclusive after three to four years of exposure. I had Zoloft 100 mg daily earlier but currently, on Paxil 40 mg and Propranolol 60 mg daily.After nearly four years of exposure and a negative antibody test four months back, would that test have detected antibodies if I were in a stage of HIV or AIDS? Do you think it was conclusive? Or is there another test I should have done? I have read about an HIV RNA test, but it says early detection. I understand that it detects more than the antibodies. What are your thoughts on my next step?
output: Hi, Welcome to Chat Doctor forum. As you describe your history, you should get evaluated for any possible opportunistic infections like TB, fungal infection etc. You should consult a physician and get evaluated for those. Regarding your question regarding HIV, In most cases, HIV testing will detect positive results within 2-8 weeks after exposure. However, some individuals can take up to 12 weeks to develop detectable levels of HIV antibodies. In rare instances, it may take longer to develop detectable levels. So, you should repeat the test again after 12 weeks. Hope I answered your query. Wishing you good health. Take care

instruction: Hello doctor,My LMP date was a month back. Yesterday, I took a pregnancy test and it came positive. Today also I repeated the test and it is also positive but in the afternoon I had dark brown little bleeding like spotting. What does it mean? Am I pregnant or not?

instruction: Hello doctor,I am 27 weeks pregnant now and by scan two weeks back and the doctor says the baby is IUGR due to placental insufficiency. She said to terminate the pregnancy but I feel baby movement and heart rate. Also, I am pre-eclamptic and diabetic but sugar is controlled. Tell me what can I do. Any treatment or way to have a healthy baby and near to due date?IUD 18 weeks, fifth-week pregnancy due to no fetal heart rate, so DNE was done. Currently, I am taking Duphaston 10 mg BD, Asgard 75 mg OD, Glucophage 500 mg TDS, and Aldomet 250 mg QID two tablets.
output: 30 weeks of pregnancy is very important for the development of your child. At this stage the fetus is not fully developed and has still some time to grow in size. The most common cause of IUGR(intrauterine growth restriction) is maternal diabetes. Other causes may be congenital anomaly, bleeding in the mother, high blood pressure during pregnancy etc. Your doctor has suggested termination of pregnancy because there is no hope of improvement in the condition of the fetus. You might consider terminating the pregnancy if you are unable to tolerate the symptoms that come with pregnancy.

instruction: Hello doctor,Is it possible for the knees and shoulder or spine growth plates to be open, once the hip and ankle growth plates have closed?
output: Yes, all long bones such as femur, humerus, radius etc. undergo growth at their respective joints. The growth is gradual and occurs in a definite sequence from proximal end towards distal end of the bone. That means first the head grows followed by neck, then shaft and lastly the trochanteric region of femur. Similarly, other bones grow in a similar manner. So yes, there can be open growth plates even if hip and ankle growth plates have already closed. Hope this helps you.

instruction: Hello doctor,I am a 19 year old boy and I have myopia (2.5 approximately in both the eyes) and I am wearing glasses since two and a half years. Now, I am thinking to quit glasses. What best can I do to reduce the power and quit glasses completely?
output: Thank you for posting your query. Myopia is an inherited condition which cannot be cured by any treatment. But if you wear glasses or contact lenses, it will help improve vision. The progression of myopia slows down after puberty and stabilizes at around age 20. So, if you stop wearing glasses, there will not be much change in your refractive error. However, if you do not want to wear spectacles, then you could go for surgical correction like LASIK or PRK. These surgeries remove tissue from the cornea to correct refractive errors. You need to consult an ophthalmologist for detailed evaluation before proceeding with such procedures. Hope this helps.

instruction: Hello doctor,My 59 year old father has hypertension from the past nine years and acidity problem. He got an acute MI last month. Prior to this, from past 10 days, he was suffering from a low blood pressure and our family doctor asked him to stop the BP tablet for a few days. At morning 5 AM, he got high acidity and chest pain, but we thought it was acidity and gave him Rantac and other home remedies. But, he started sweating and got severe pain in the chest. We took him to a nearby hospital and the doctor immediately did the angiography and found the main coronary artery was 100 % blocked which had to be stented immediately. But, he said it is very risky as you have reached late. The damage has already happened. He processed with the angioplasty. There were a total of three blockages on the left side. Two were done via balloon and the 100 % blockage one was stented. Post the surgery, on the next day, my dad started feeling high acidity, big burps, and heaviness in the chest and his heart rate was very high. From then, we were in the hospital for ten days until his heart rate and BP and other things got normal. He had little breathlessness also.Post returning home, he felt very weak and again a week later, he got readmitted for low blood pressure as my dad fainted at home and we checked the BP was very low and hence we got him to the hospital. The doctors admitted him to the ICCU and started giving fluids to bring up his BP. The doctors said low BP was due to dehydration as my father had gone for motions thrice that particular morning and since the intake of fluids is restricted to 1.5 liters max.Previous medication when we got discharged: Cardivas, Ivabrad, Ecosprin, Brilinta, Restyl for sleep and now since my dad complained of breathlessness, they have changed the medication and now they have discontinued Cardivas completely and increased the dose of Ivabrad and asked to stop Brilinta and take Prax 10 mg. My query is should one discontinue Cardivas abruptly in between? Also, his heart rate is very fluctuating and at times his respiratory rate also reaches 25 to 30 at times. And his LVEF on the day of discharge was 30 to 35 % but on the day when he got readmitted his LVEF was 25 to 30 %. Is the heart muscle becoming too weak? What could be the reason for the same? Please advice.
output: 1) Cardivas is a calcium channel blocker (CCB). CCB like Cardivas should not be stopped suddenly as it may lead to hypotension or bradycardia. It is better to taper down the doses gradually over a period of time by reducing the dose every alternate day. 2) LVEF is the measure of how much pumping power your heart has. If your LVEF is less than 40%, then there is a possibility of congestive cardiac failure (CCF). CCF occurs when the heart can no longer effectively fill with blood during diastole i.e. when the heart relaxes after each contraction. This happens because the heart muscle becomes too weak to contract well. You need to get an echocardiogram done to know more about your heart function.

instruction: Hello doctor,My issue is related to skin color. Of late I have been observing that there is a change in the color (white) at the shaft (penis) as well as the skin below. output: Hi, thank you for posting your query. The white discoloration of penile skin could be due to vitiligo or psoriasis. Vitiligo is an autoimmune condition wherein the immune system attacks the pigment producing cells called melanocytes. As these cells are destroyed, white patches appear on the skin. Psoriasis is another condition which causes thickening of the skin with scaling. It can also affect the genitals. Both conditions can cause white patches on the shaft of the penis as well as the skin below. You need to get yourself evaluated by a dermatologist who will examine you clinically and prescribe medicines accordingly. Hope this information was useful. Best wishes.

instruction: Dear doctor,Which is the primary blood test for HIV? Is it fasting or nonfasting? I want to get tested for a routine checkup.
output: Non-Fasting Blood Test for HIV. The primary blood test for HIV is called "ELISA". This test can be done either as a fasting or non-fasting test. The ELISA test is performed by taking a small sample of your blood and then running it through a machine that detects antibodies against HIV. These antibodies are produced by your body in response to the virus. Once these antibodies are detected in your blood, they remain there even if you take medications to treat HIV. Therefore, this test can be used to determine whether you have been infected with HIV. It also gives an indication of how long ago you were exposed to HIV. An additional test called Western Blot is usually performed at the same time as ELISA. It is more sensitive than ELISA and will give a much more accurate result. However, most doctors use the ELISA test

instruction: Hi doctor,I am trying to find out a specific function of the diaphragm when it comes to taking a deep breath. output: Hi, Thank you for asking Chat Doctor. I have gone through your query and would try to help you in the best possible way. The diaphragm does play an important role in breathing. The diaphragm contracts and relaxes during respiration. During inspiration, it is pulled downward by the lungs, thus increasing the volume of the thoracic cavity and pushing the abdominal organs upwards. This movement causes the rib cage to expand and allows air to enter the lungs. During expiration, the diaphragm is relaxed and pushed upwards by the abdomen, thus decreasing the size of the thoracic cavity and pressing the abdominal organs into the chest cavity. This causes the pressure inside the chest cavity to decrease, allowing air to be exhaled out. Hope this helps. Let me know if I can assist you further.

instruction: Hello doctor,Is HIV RNA, QL TMA accurate after 20 to 21 days of exposure? And also this came with my results. RNA is not detected. No laboratory evidence of HIV infection. The HIV-1 RNA qualitative TMA assay is recommended for use as part of a multi-test HIV-1/HIV-2 screening and diagnostic algorithm. This assay can also be used to resolve indeterminate HIV-1 antibody assay results, and to test for HIV-1 infection in patients less than 2 years old. When a fourth generation HIV multi-test screening and diagnostic algorithm is used, if the test results include a repeatedly reactive HIV-1/2 antigen/antibody (fourth generation) screen, followed by negative confirmatory tests for HIV-1 and 2 antibodies and HIV-1 RNA by TMA, the most likely interpretation is a non-specific (biological false positive) reaction in the fourth generation screening assay. instruction: Hello doctor,My little daughter has a supravalvular pulmonary membrane that causes minimal stenosis. So I do not know what to do. output: Hi thanks for posting your query in Chat Doctor. Supravalvular pulmonary stenosis is commonly diagnosed in childhood. It is usually associated with other congenital heart diseases like ventricular septal defect or atrial septal defect. In some cases it may present as an isolated finding. Treatment of choice is open heart surgery which is called Glenn procedure. It consists of division of interventricular septum between right and left ventricles and creation of a new pathway between right and left lung. This allows blood from upper lobes of lungs to pass into left side of heart and then out through aorta. Thus it helps to increase oxygenation of blood. Surgical repair can also be done by using catheterization techniques under fluoroscopy guidance. I hope you find my answer helpful. Wishing your baby good health.

My front four teeth shifted a lot (they are crowded, so it was a quite visible shift, some were pushed out, and some pushed back).The retainer could make a big difference in one night when I wore it, but I was advised to get a completely new brace. So a few days ago, I got a lingual brace on the front teeth (the social six). My concern now is the speed of shifting. A couple of hours after getting the braces, my teeth were significantly straighter (1 to 2 mm difference).A day after they look almost perfect, I was told I would be wearing the braces for six months to a year. How is such a drastic change possible so quickly, and is it healthy or normal? It hurts always, but it is not unbearable. And could I have used a new retainer instead of getting new braces then? I hope you can help with my worries.
output: Hi, Thanks for writing to Chat Doctor. Braces work by applying pressure on the teeth. This pressure causes movement of the teeth in the direction of the force applied. The faster the pressure is applied and maintained, the faster will be the movement of the teeth. In your case, the dentist has applied the pressure at higher levels. The force is also maintained for longer duration. Since the teeth were already moving, this process accelerated the movement. You should continue with the treatment for another 6 months to see complete results. Regards

The exact cause of keratoconus is unknown but may be due to genetics or environmental factors. There is no cure for keratoconus but treatments can help slow down its progression and reduce symptoms such as distorted vision. They provide a large, gas permeable contact lens that fits over your entire cornea and provides a smooth, comfortable fit that can correct vision problems caused by keratoconus. instruction: Hi doctor,I was diagnosed with Asperger syndrome when I was 13 years of age. I am 22 now. How does the DSM-5 change that disorder?
output: The DSM-V has changed its criteria for AS. It is no longer considered to be an autism spectrum disorder but rather a separate diagnosis in itself. The new diagnostic criteria include deficits in social communication and restricted interests or activities. It also includes significant impairments in nonverbal behaviors, such as eye contact and facial expressions, which were not included under the previous criteria. There are other changes as well, such as the elimination of stereotyped behavior and repetitive motor movements.

instruction: Hi doctor, My husband was diagnosed with APL before six years. He underwent treatment by following the pethema protocol for APL. After consolidation phase, BMA revealed there is still 7% of PML Rara using fish rara test while negative on cytogenetics. His doctor proceeded to his maintenance phase two years on ATRA, Mercaptopurine, and Methotrexate. For two years monitoring blood counts are within the normal range. BMA was done this year and revealed there is still 3% on FISH Rara. Is this considered a minimal residual disease? Or incomplete remission? Does he need to undergo chemo again or start a new ATRA?
output: 100% recovery from Acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL) does not occur in majority of patients.  The current standard of care is to maintain the patient on low dose ATRA and chemotherapy(all-trans retinoic acid [ATRA] + anthracyclines/cytosine analogues) until complete remission (CR) is achieved.  CR is defined as absence of blast cells in peripheral blood and bone marrow.  Persistent minimal residual disease (MRD) may be present even after achieving CR. MRD levels can only be detected by molecular methods such as PCR or FISH.  It has been suggested that if MRD levels are less than 1%, then it is likely that the disease is in full remission.  In your husbands case, since the MRD levels are above 1%, further treatment is required.

instruction: Hello doctor,I am 20 years old, type 2 diabetes patient. Please give me information about diabetes. Every morning, I do running around 2 to 3 km.

instruction: Hello doctor,Can one be color blind if one has 20/20 vision?
output: 1. No, not at all, but it is possible to have normal vision and still be color blind. Color blindness is an inherited condition that affects the way certain colors appear to people with this condition. It is caused by problems in the cells of the retina that respond to light.  The cells are called cones. People who are color blind usually cannot distinguish shades of red, green or blue. Someone with this condition may also have difficulty seeing yellow, brown, and gray. Color blindness can be passed down from parents to their children.

While the pain is not yet excruciating it is still very bothersome and uncomfortable. I could compare the feeling to beg deeply bruised. It almost feels like I was kicked hard in the abdomen and back. I am dealing with something autoimmune but right now it is labeled as UCTD (undifferentiated connective tissue disease). I think it could be related. My concern is that it could be pancreatitis. Do I need to go to the ER? Does pancreatitis progress slowly? This is day two and I do not want to get to the point of excruciating pain.
output: Hi, Thanks for writing your query at Chat Doctor. Pain in the left side of the chest, which wraps around to back, can be due to many causes. In your case it can be due to pancreatitis. Since you are already having autoimmune problem (ulcerative colitis) the chance of pancreatitis is more likely. Pancreatitis presents with severe pain in the central part of the upper abdomen. The pain is sharp, usually occurs after eating, and may last for few hours. The pain radiates to the back. There is also vomiting associated with it. The commonest cause for pancreatitis is gall stones. So if you are having these symptoms then get yourself evaluated by your doctor. Get ultrasound done to rule out gall stones. Hope this information helps you. Take care.

instruction: Hello doctor,My creatinine level is 2.0. What is the best medication?
output: 1) In acute renal failure, the patients usually have a high BP and edema, which is due to retention of sodium and water in the body. The cause for this retention can be any form of kidney disease or any other disease process that affects the kidneys like diabetes, lupus, amyloidosis etc.2) Management of such patients involves close monitoring of blood pressure and water and salt intake.3) Patients who are not able to take adequate amount of fluids will need some form of dialysis either peritoneal or hemodialysis.4) For those with mild to moderate renal function impairment, medications like spironolactone, triamterene, amlodipine, losartan etc. can help to reduce blood pressure and improve fluid status.5) For more advanced cases, dialysis may be required.

instruction: Hello doctor,  I have a question about my soon to be 12-year-old son. Since he was 1 year old he has had febrile seizures about once a year. They only happen at night. When he is sick during the day I would give him Motrin or Tylenol. Through out the night and he would not have any symptoms. When he did not show signs of being sick that night his fever would spike. Two years ago we had his first video EEG and there were no abnormalities or no concerns. We did MRI, blood tests, and EKG all are normal. He had two seizures this year both while being sick. So the neurologist wanted another EEG. So we did a video EEG. The first night nothing looked wrong so she wanted to keep him another night. During the day he was getting sick he was running a little fever. So that night they choose not to give him Motrin to see if he would have a seizure and he did. It lasted a minute and was a full-body one. They looked over the tape and said there was no evidence of one coming on it came so quickly. They believe (but are not sure) that it came from the frontal lobe. They put him on Keppra for two weeks and then the doctor looked it over with her partners and they decide that Trileptal and Keppra would be what he needs. I happen to total disagree. He has never had a seizure during the day or one without a fever. I feel they so quickly diagnosed him with epilepsy without considering that all his tests are normal. That seizure they saw came on because we didn\t give him medicine for his fever. Which to me seems like he has the rare case of febrile seizures lasting till the age of 12 years. He did not have any seizures last year but just two seizures this year. I personally want to try and build his immune system to stop him from getting sick to see if that will prevent his seizures. His father disagrees with me and agrees with the doctor. I believe the side effects of both these medicine out way the actual problem. I am just overwhelmed and stressed. Because I do not know what is the right thing to do? Can febrile seizures last to the age of 12? Is it rare for someone to have a seizure maybe once a year then not have any, then have one the next year? Does the medicine he is on sound too extreme? Please advise.
output: Hi, I understand your concern regarding your sons health problems. However, in my opinion, epilepsy should be considered as a possibility even if the other investigations are normal. At least an EEG should be done to rule out epilepsy and other possible causes. As far as febrile seizures are concerned, they usually occur between 6 months and 5 years of age and rarely after that. However, they can recur in childhood, adolescence and even adult life. In your sons case, since he is around 12 years of age, it is unlikely that he will continue to have seizures unless it is due to some underlying cause which may be identified by further investigation. Hopefully, this information helps you make an informed decision regarding treatment of your son. Best wishes,

instruction: Hello doctor,My brother has thalassemia intermedia. His Hb is between 7.8 to 9. Please suggest how soon he can recover from this.
output: Hello, Thanks for writing in to us. Thalassemia Intermedia is an inherited disorder of hemoglobin synthesis and it is also known as Mediterranean Anemia. It is characterized by increased erythropoiesis (production of red blood cells) and reduced life span of RBCs. The treatment consists of regular transfusions, iron chelation therapy, folic acid supplementation and splenectomy when indicated. Treatment for thalassemia should be started early in childhood. The aim of treatment is to reduce or eliminate the need for frequent transfusion.

instruction: Hi doctor,I have a few doubts regarding annual flu vaccine. Is it a must to get an annual vaccine shot every year? Is it mandatory for kids? output: Hi, dear thanks for your question. Influenza (flu) is a contagious disease caused by influenza viruses that affects the respiratory tract. It causes fever, sore throat, headache, muscle pain, congestion, runny nose and coughing. The best way to prevent getting sick with flu is to get the flu vaccination each year. Flu shots can protect against three different flu viruses. Vaccines are available in the form of injections and nasal sprays. Flu shots are usually given as an injection into the muscle of the arm or sometimes into the skin of the shoulder area. Flu shots are recommended for everyone over 6 months old. Flu shots are especially important for people who are at high risk of serious complications from the flu, including young children, pregnant women, people with chronic illnesses such as diabetes

If this is the case than the fluid needs to be removed surgically.3) The third option is that there is nothing wrong but the child is just not able to hear well. output: 1) Glaucoma is defined by optic nerve damage. This can be detected by imaging the optic nerve (OCT). It also can be detected by testing visual field function. If your visual fields are normal then the glaucoma diagnosis should be questioned.2) The other thing that needs to be considered is whether the glaucoma is open angle or closed angle. Closed angle glaucoma is more severe than open angle glaucoma and is treated differently. Open angle glaucoma is usually treated with medications. Closed angle glaucoma is usually treated with laser surgery. You would want to make sure that the correct type of glaucoma is being treated.3) Eye pressure monitoring is important but it does not determine treatment. It may tell you if you are getting better or worse but it does not tell you how much pressure reduction is needed for successful treatment.4) T

instruction: Hello doctor,What is raw water and how is it different from the tap, spring, and other types of water? What are the perceived benefits and dangers of drinking raw water? When did this fad start? Have you ever seen a patient getting sick by drinking raw water?
output: Hi there, Raw water is water that has not been treated in any way. It comes straight from its source - usually groundwater or surface water such as lakes and streams. Unlike treated water which goes through a process of filtration and chemical treatment to make it safe for human consumption, raw water does not undergo any of these processes. This means that it may contain bacteria, viruses, parasites and other organisms that can cause illness if consumed. The most common risks associated with consuming raw water are gastrointestinal illnesses like diarrhea, vomiting, and cramps. In rare cases, more serious diseases such as typhoid fever, Cholera, hepatitis A, and polio have also been reported. There are no health benefits associated with drinking raw water. The only benefit it offers is that it is natural and untreated. The practice of drinking raw water

instruction: Results from an HSG procedure showed that I have a bicornuate uterus or a thick septum. Both Fallopian tubes are patent. But there is an abnormal position of the uterine body, possibly due to a cystic nodularity in the right adnexa, displacing the entire uterine body toward the left side of the pelvic cavity. Currently trying to conceive and I\m pretty concerned about the complications with both fertility and pregnancy due to the potential above diagnosis. Further clinical evaluation is recommended. What can be done to fix this and/or make the changes for a healthy full-term pregnancy? Thanks!
output: Yes, if your HSG shows a bicornuate uterus then it means that your uterus is not shaped normally. The normal shape for a female is like a tulip with two flaps at the top which are called cornua. You may have one or two cornua missing as well as a thin wall between the two halves of your uterus. This makes conception difficult because the sperm cannot swim up the fallopian tubes to reach the egg. It also means that if you do become pregnant, the baby will not develop properly in the first months of its life. The best way to correct this problem is to have surgery to remove the wall between the two sides of your uterus and reconnect the two sides. This is called a hysterosalpingogram (HSG). You should discuss this operation with your gynecologist.

instruction: Hello doctor,I have wolf Parkinson white syndrome. I was admitted to a hospital last week and was discharged within one day. The doctor said that first, we can check through medicine, now sometimes I am feeling nervous and minute rapid heartbeat.
output: Hi, Welcome to Chat Doctor forum. Wolf-Parkinson White (WPW) is an extra conduction pathway in which there is direct connection between atria and ventricles. Please consult your cardiologist for further management. Thanks.

instruction: Hello doctor,Four months ago, I consulted you on this platform for premature complexes which I was having without any other symptoms. How to get rid of this unwanted health anxiety which I have got into?

However, if you are not taking enough protein rich foods, then you are more likely to suffer from muscular weakness and pain.3) Health anxiety is very common among people who have chronic illnesses, especially those that are difficult to diagnose. This is because people with such conditions worry that they might develop serious complications that would require major treatment. It is important to understand that anxiety is a normal reaction to a stressful situation. It actually helps us to cope better and focus on what we need to do. Your eye pressure is fine and you should discuss with your ophthalmologist regarding the medication that you are taking.

output: Hey, Thanks for writing in. Pheochromocytomas are tumors that arise from chromaffin cells found in certain areas of body like adrenal glands. output: I hope I am able to answer most of your concerns. Firstly, I would not recommend going for pregnancy immediately after a negative ANA result. instruction: Hi doctor,What is Rhesus? My wife is pregnant and started clinic today.
output: Hi, I am Chat Doctor.  I have read your question and understand your concerns. Let me try to help you Question : What is Rhesus? Answer :Rhesus (Rh) factor is an inherited blood trait that affects how your body responds to certain diseases. It is one of the most common inherited factors in humans. It is also known as the Rhesus Factor or RH factor. The Rh factor is determined by whether or not you have inherited rhesus positive antigens from your mother. The Rh factor is usually detected through a simple blood test called the Rh factor test. Rhesus negative individuals do not have these antigens and therefore can receive Rh positive blood without any problems. Rhesus positive individuals may develop antibodies against Rh-positive red blood cells, which can cause problems for subsequent pregnancies. Please tell me how gestational age will be calculated from LMP or conception day? I am not sure when I ovulated? Please help me out.
output: 1) The gestation age is calculated by the last menstrual period (LMP). The exact date of conception is not known, but it is generally assumed to have occurred around the time of ovulation. This is usually about two weeks before the next expected menses. 2) In case of missed abortion, you should take an opinion from a gynecologist and get a scan done. A complete hysteroscopy and biopsy may be needed. 3) If there is any doubt regarding the viability of the fetus, then you can undergo a surgical procedure called as dilatation and curettage (D & C) to remove the contents of the uterus.

instruction: Hi doctor,My wife is pregnant with twins, 24 weeks now. Her Hb levels never in life had gone above 10. At the start of pregnancy, it was 8.5 but now it has touched 7.7. We did serum ferritin test and her level was 50 (normal) which I guess means no iron deficiency. She is a beta thalassemia minor as per the detailed reports. Can you please guide here? Our gynecologist would be consulting a hematologist today but if we can get an opinion here it would be great.
output: 1. It is true that iron requirement is increased during pregnancy by about 30-60 mg/day. This is due to increase in hemoglobin production and blood volume.2. Ferritin is the protein storage form of iron and is not sufficient for iron requirements. You need to have serum iron, total iron binding capacity and transferrin saturation to assess adequacy of iron stores.3. Beta thalassemia is a genetic condition where there is reduced synthesis of hemoglobin. The treatment is lifelong transfusion therapy. Intrauterine transfusions may also be required. There are certain medications that can help control the transfusion requirements. Consult your hematologist for further guidance.

output: 2nd trimester ultrasonography can also detect fetal heart activity. This will be done by your gynecologist or obstetrician. The ultrasonographer may hear the fetal heartbeat with a Doppler device, but this is not always reliable. It is important that the ultrasonographer knows how many weeks of pregnancy you are at when they do the scan. This is because the baby grows at different rates during different stages of pregnancy. The size of the fetus and its position in relation to the placenta are important information to determine whether or not the pregnancy is viable. It is possible that your ultrasonographer did not know that you were at 4 months of gestation before doing the scan.

Is it wise if I take a second dose of the pill to completely reduce chances of implantation? Is it safe to take a higher dose of pills to completely eradicate any possibility of pregnancy?2. What else can I do to make sure I am completely out of the woods?3. Also, after seven days, is it okay for me to start taking antibiotics to eradicate any infections passed? Can general antibiotics like Amoxil treat the treatable STI?4. When is the most prudent time to take an HIV test?5. How effective is P2 when taken during ovulation? Is it guarantee that if it delays I am pregnant? Is it also possible for me to have my period yet still be pregnant?10. Lastly, what are the chances in terms of percentage that I might be pregnant without necessarily having penetrative intercourse?
output: 1. The emergency contraceptive pill is only 75-89% effective in preventing a pregnancy. It is best used as soon as possible after unprotected sex, but you may take it up to 72 hours after unprotected sex. You would need to use another form of birth control for the rest of your cycle until you have regular menstrual cycles again.2. The antibiotic will not treat STIs unless they are bacterial rather than viral.3. You can start taking antibiotics at any time if you suspect an infection.4. HIV testing should be done immediately after potential exposure.5. Emergency contraception has varying effectiveness depending upon the stage of your cycle. It is usually more effective earlier in the cycle.6. A chemical abortion can be induced by medications, but it is not considered safe.7. Pregnancy tests cannot detect a pregnancy

output: 19 days is considered safe period for unprotected sex in women who have regular cycles (i.e., with same duration and interval between two successive cycles). instruction: Hi doctor,I am on CPAP for two years and my AHI is in normal limits. But, the quality of my sleep is not good. My body and brain are not at all relaxing during sleep. I have aching muscles. Please guide.
output: Hi there, AHI is the number of times your breathing stops or reduces to such an extent that it causes you to wake up from sleep. This is measured by a device called a Sleep Study or Polysomnogram (PSG). The PSG records your heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, respiration rate, limb movements etc. It also measures your airflow and breathing effort through a mask and recording the flow of air into and out of the nose. In addition, it records eye movement, leg movements, arm movements, and brain waves. If all this data shows that your breathing stops more than 5 times per hour then you will be diagnosed with Obstructive Sleep Apnea Syndrome (OSAS). OSAS is a condition where the tongue falls back against the soft palate and blocks the airway, causing pauses in breathing while asleep. OSAS can cause daytime fatigue

output: 1) As you mentioned your age is 20 years, so there may be possibility of hormonal imbalance due to stress or anxiety. So please consult gynecologist for diagnosis and treatment. 2) You can take tab. Ovral-G (Mifepristone 200 mg + Tab. Betahistine 4 mg) tablet for induction of period. Take one tablet daily for 3 days after period missed. 3) It will also prevent unwanted pregnancy.

instruction: Hello doctor,I am a 34 year old male working as an engineer. Regarding my mental state, I feel lethargic and sleepy all day. I do not have the interest to do anything in life. I have lost interest even in my favorite activities. I consulted a psychiatrist and he diagnosed it as major depressive disorder with OCD traits and hypertension. But, I do not want to take medicines unless I know for sure it is really going to cure me. Please help.
output: 1) You need to be treated aggressively. 2) You may have symptoms of obsessive compulsive disorder (OCD). 3) Treating your depression will also treat your OCD symptoms. 4) Depression is a serious illness that requires treatment. 5) Medication can help you control your symptoms. 6) Talk therapy (psychotherapy) can help you learn how to cope with depression and its related problems. 7) There are several types of antidepressant medications, so your doctor may try different ones until they find one that works best for you.8) Your doctor may add a medicine called a benzodiazepine to help with anxiety.9) Exercise regularly and eat healthily.

instruction: Hi doctor,I am a 49 year old female. My resting heart rate is 69 bpm. What should be my target heart rate during physical activity?
output: 100-120bpm is normal range of heart rate for an adult in rest state. During moderate or vigorous exercise, the heart rate increases by 20-30 bpm above resting rate and at maximum exercise it may increase up to 200 bpm. So you need to keep in mind that your heart rate should not exceed 175 bpm while exercising.

So, if you were already in the first half of the menstrual cycle when you had unprotected intercourse then chances of conception were high. So get a urine pregnancy test done at home as soon as possible (it will give you an early detection) & consult gynecologist for further evaluation.

Other causes include injury or disease such as glaucoma, cataracts, retinitis pigmentosa, optic nerve diseases, and diabetes. The most common type of colorblindness is red-green color blinding and affects about 8 percent of men and 0.5 percent of women. There are many types of color blindness, including blue-yellow color blindness and total color blindness. instruction: Hello doctor,I am trying to understand how a Coombs test would be used to diagnose me for cold-agglutinin-disease. Can you please help explain in understandable terms what that would do? I am confused between direct and indirect tests.
output: Hi there, thanks for your question. A coombs test is done to see if antibodies have been produced against red blood cells. These antibodies are called "coombs" antibodies. They can present in different diseases like cold agglutinin disease, autoimmune hemolytic anemia etc. The test has two parts -direct and indirect. In direct test, RBCs are incubated with serum from the patient, and then tested for agglutination (clumping) of RBCs. Indirect test involves mixing of RBCs with normal serum, and then adding the patients serum. This test is more sensitive than direct test, but less specific. So if you have a positive result, it means that you should consult a hematologist as soon as possible for further work up. Hope this helps.

instruction: Hello doctor,Can you please tell me what is the difference between thoracic, thoracolumbar and lumbar fusion? Or are they all the same?
output: Thoracic fusion is performed to fuse the vertebrae in the middle of the spine (thoracic region). The goal of this surgery is to prevent painful motion in the spine and create stability. Lumbar fusion is also performed to fuse two or more vertebral levels together. However, it is usually done for degenerative disc disease that causes back pain. In lumbar fusion, the bones are stabilized with metal rods and screws. The spinal canal is not reduced in size as it would be during a thoracic fusion.

instruction: Hello doctor,What is the time period that HIV virus will be detected in blood by using available test methods? Please give minimum and maximum time period details.

This means that if someone has been exposed to HIV, they should wait at least three months before having an HIV test. The most accurate way to detect HIV is through PCR testing. instruction: Hello doctor,Do my spirometry results tell you anything? Are they below normal? I am a male 175 cm, 83 kg, 39 years old. I sometimes have shortness of breath.

The results are expressed as FEV1 (Forced Expiratory Volume in One Second) and FVC (Forced Vital Capacity). Normal values vary from lab to lab but usually fall between 80%-120% of predicted value. So, if you want more details about your spirometry results, you may send them to me as a direct question. Hope this answers your query. Wish you good health.

instruction: Hello doctor,I had protected sexual intercourse five months back. Now tested for STD and everything came back negative. I have a question around HSV. HSV index value for type 1 is 0.70 and type 2 is 0.23. It was a type specific IgG antibody test. Is this result conclusive? Or do I need to retake at any point of time in the future? Your response is most appreciated.
output: Hi, Welcome to Chat Doctor forum. The Herpes Simplex Virus (HSV) is a virus that can cause genital herpes. There are two types of herpes simplex virus (HSV), HSV-1 and HSV-2. Both types can cause sores or blisters in and around the mouth and on the face, but only HSV-2 can cause sores in and around the vagina and anus. Most people get HSV-2 when they are sexually active with someone who has the virus. It is important to know if you have HSV-1 or HSV-2 because the medicines used to treat it are different. Testing for HSV-1 and HSV-2 involves taking a blood sample. The results of these tests will be available after about four weeks. If you have been exposed to either HSV-1 or HSV-2, then you should be tested every six months

output: Hello, Thanks for your query. I understand your concern. Sleepwalking is a disorder in which people get up from bed while asleep and walk around.
